title: Hearing Bix play open horn and dumping his mutes
summary: Hearing Bix Beiderbecke with the Wolverines convinces him to abandon mutes; Bix's big, fat sound and his Bach cornet.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Well, at the end of that summer-- he was always telling me that he knew Bix and that Bix was out in the Stockton Club -- and that I would be--- and, you know, that I would really like the way he plays but I had heard him play in there somewhere, playing a dance at a college and I heard him play and I couldn't believe--- of course, I had played the trumpet in those days with a lot of muted things -

Yeah - and I hated those damn mutes - I really did. And, then I heard the Wolverines and I heard him play open horn and I--- that's the last mute for me. When I heard him play that open horn, I just dumped my mutes.

That was a revelation for Bix--- was three years older than you were so by the time you heard him he was pretty well developed --- and this is true - that was his big revelation - wasn't it - for all trumpet players---

Oh, to hear this guy - he was so far ahead of us all. You know, he was miles ahead of everybody. And, with that sound - he got a beautiful, big, fat sound out of his cornet, you know and I remember--- I even remember the kind of a horn it was. He played a Bach --
